Secure Boot.rationale: Secure Boot enforces cryptographic verification of early-stage bootloaders and firmware prior to execution. ECDSA P-256 is optimal for constrained MCUs, while RSA-3072 enables faster verification where boot-time latency is critical.
Secure Boot.securityLifespan: Secure until ~2030 (RSA/ECDSA). State-machine tracking or PQC transition required for 15+ year lifespans.
riskFlags: Vulnerable to quantum Shor's algorithm over long-term lifespans (>15 years)
Boot latency overhead when utilizing large PQC public keys
Secure Boot.pqcMigrationPath: Transition to stateful hash-based signatures (LMS/HSS per NIST SP 800-208) or lattice-based ML-DSA (FIPS 204) for long-lived automotive platforms.

OTA Update.recommendedAlgorithm: Ed25519 or ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 / SHA-3-256
OTA Update.rationale: OTA updates require resilient signature verification under severe asymmetric bandwidth constraints. Dual-signing / hybrid verification allows immediate transition to PQC roots of trust.
OTA Update.securityLifespan: Classical signatures valid until ~2030; PQC hybrid roots mandatory for UNECE R156 compliance across 15-20 year fleets.
riskFlags: Shor's algorithm breaks classical signature verification
Firmware rollback vulnerability if monotonic version counters are absent
OTA Update.pqcMigrationPath: Implement hybrid signature wrapping (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) with Uptane compliant multi-repository key delegation.

V2X Communication.recommendedAlgorithm: ECDSA P-256 / BrainpoolP256r1 with IEEE 1609.2 / ETSI TS 103 097
V2X Communication.rationale: High message frequency and strict millisecond-level verification latency require compact signatures and hardware acceleration.
V2X Communication.securityLifespan: Classical mechanisms secure short-to-medium term (~2030); strict latency limits currently challenge PQC message size integration.
riskFlags: Quantum harvest-and-forge exposure
PQC signature bandwidth overhead on IEEE 802.11p/C-V2X channels
V2X Communication.pqcMigrationPath: Evaluate lightweight stateful or lattice signatures (Falcon-512) to fit IEEE 1609.2 MTU limits.

SecOC / In-Vehicle Communication.rationale: In-vehicle CAN / CAN-FD networks have constrained payload limits. AES-CMAC (truncated to 24-64 bits) paired with freshness values provides low-latency bus integrity.
SecOC / In-Vehicle Communication.securityLifespan: Resistant to quantum Shor's attack. Grover's algorithm halves symmetric space; 128-bit remains safe against practical online bus attacks.
riskFlags: Truncated MAC collision probability if freshness counters reset
Insecure symmetric key distribution across ECUs
SecOC / In-Vehicle Communication.pqcMigrationPath: Upgrade symmetric key lengths to 256-bit (AES-256-CMAC) during next-generation HSM refresh; no architectural overhaul required.

ECU-to-ECU Communication.recommendedAlgorithm: AES-128-GCM or AES-256-GCM with SOME/IP-SD Security
ECU-to-ECU Communication.pqcCandidate: Hybrid ECDH + ML-KEM-768 for session key establishment
ECU-to-ECU Communication.rationale: High-bandwidth Ethernet/SOME-IP communication between zonal controllers requires wire-speed confidentiality and authenticated integrity.
ECU-to-ECU Communication.securityLifespan: Secure past 2035 for symmetric traffic; ephemeral key exchange must account for quantum interception.
riskFlags: Replay and reflection attacks without cryptographic session freshness
ECU-to-ECU Communication.pqcMigrationPath: Transition session handshakes to ML-KEM (Kyber) via TLS 1.3 hybrid cipher suites.

Key Exchange.rationale: Pure classical Diffie-Hellman / ECDH is directly compromised by Shor's algorithm. For vehicles lasting 15-20 years, Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) necessitates hybrid post-quantum key encapsulation.
Key Exchange.securityLifespan: Hybrid scheme secure against both classical and quantum adversaries through 2045+.
riskFlags: Immediate HNDL threat on all stored telematics and diagnostics session traffic
Higher RAM requirements during lattice polynomial expansion
Key Exchange.pqcMigrationPath: Deploy hybrid ECDH + ML-KEM-768 immediately for all backhaul, telematics, and diagnostics key exchange channels.

Data Encryption.rationale: Symmetric encryption using AES-256 offers 128 bits of post-quantum security against Grover's algorithm, satisfying long-term retention requirements for crash logs and telematics data.
riskFlags: IV/Nonce reuse catastrophic vulnerability in GCM mode
Unauthenticated CBC mode exposure to padding oracle exploits
Data Encryption.pqcMigrationPath: Ensure default 256-bit key length across all storage domains; algorithm replacement is not required.

Digital Signatures.pqcCandidate: ML-DSA-65 / ML-DSA-87 (NIST FIPS 204) or SLH-DSA (NIST FIPS 205)
Digital Signatures.rationale: Digital signatures are required for certificate issuance, diagnostic authorization, and telemetry signing. Lifespans exceeding 10 years must prepare for lattice-based schemes.
riskFlags: Retroactive signature forgery if public key certificates outlive classical security margin
Digital Signatures.pqcMigrationPath: Deploy dual-cert infrastructure supporting standard X.509 v3 with PQC extensions.

RNG.recommendedAlgorithm: Hardware TRNG seeded into NIST SP 800-90A CTR_DRBG (AES-256)
RNG.rationale: Cryptographic unpredictability underpins keys, nonces, and session tokens. Automotive MCUs must leverage HSM hardware entropy with continuous online health tests.
RNG.securityLifespan: Long-term certified if hardware noise sources conform to SP 800-90B.
riskFlags: Entropy starvation during early cold-boot cycles
Undetected hardware oscillator drift or physical fault injection
RNG.pqcMigrationPath: RNG architectures remain quantum-safe provided minimum 256 bits of real entropy are extracted.

Diagnostics (UDS).pqcCandidate: TLS 1.3 with Hybrid ML-KEM + ML-DSA Authorization
Diagnostics (UDS).rationale: Unified Diagnostic Services over IP (DoIP) require mutual authentication and role-based access control to prevent unauthorized ECU flashing and calibration changes.
Diagnostics (UDS).securityLifespan: Legacy seed-key (0x27) is obsolete. Service 0x29 asymmetric authentication valid to ~2030+.
riskFlags: Brute-force vulnerabilities in legacy seed-key algorithms
Unauthenticated diagnostic commands on internal test networks
Diagnostics (UDS).pqcMigrationPath: Upgrade diagnostic gateway to TLS 1.3 supporting hybrid quantum-safe certificate verification.

Key Management.recommendedAlgorithm: HSM-backed Storage with AES-256 Key Wrapping (NIST SP 800-38F)
Key Management.rationale: Automotive keys must be shielded from readback attacks across all vehicle operational and maintenance phases. Keys must be securely wrapped during provisioning and over-the-air updates.
riskFlags: Unencrypted debug port access (JTAG/SWD) exposing keys in plaintext RAM
Static factory master keys shared across vehicle fleets
Key Management.pqcMigrationPath: Design key storage envelopes with crypto-agility to store variable-length PQC private keys.
